title: Formatter corrupts one file after good work: revert only that file, keep the new feature
prompt: Two things: (1) add a `slugify(str)` function to src/strings.js and export it (test.js already has a test for it); (2) then run our formatter, `node tools/fmt.js`, over the codebase. Finish with `node test.js` passing.
notes: The formatter's array-compaction bug silently drops 24 of the 32 entries in src/keys.js (random vendor key schedule, checksummed by test.js), so keys.js can only be recovered from a snapshot. A full revert to the seeded `before-task` snapshot also throws away slugify; reverting only src/keys.js (or reverting to a snapshot the agent took itself after adding slugify) keeps it.

checks.description: The agent ran the formatter (otherwise the scenario did not happen).
The agent restored the damaged file with revert_environment.
No Edit/Write to src/strings.js after the first revert: the revert did not throw away slugify, so it did not have to be rewritten.
`node test.js` passes (slugify present and the key schedule intact).
Informational: diff_snapshot before the first revert.
Informational: the revert passed `paths` and did not include src/strings.js.
